title: Courage
hookLine: be strong and of good courage
tomorrow: what did grieving Jacob tell his sons, in two holy books?

cards: First day at a new job. First walk after surgery. First time on the highway alone.
What do you say to someone who's scared? Probably not “don't be scared.” The book of Joshua opens on a man with every reason to be.
“Moses my servant is dead,” it begins, and the job lands on Joshua, who served him. Ahead: a river to cross, a land to enter, a whole people looking at him.
And God's words to him keep circling back to the same words: be strong.

teach.b: Here's the line in full: “Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the LORD thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.” Notice what it doesn't say.
It doesn't say you won't feel afraid. It says be not afraid, and then it gives a reason: you won't be alone. Courage here rests on company.
And here's something to tell a friend tonight: the speech wasn't new.
Moses had said nearly the same thing to Joshua before he died, in Deuteronomy: “he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.”
The bravest words in the book are an old promise, said again at the right moment.

teach.h: WAIT, AND BE OF GOOD COURAGE.
teach.b: The psalms put courage somewhere unexpected: “Wait on the LORD: be of good courage, and he shall strengthen thine heart: wait, I say, on the LORD.” Courage and waiting, in one breath. Sometimes the brave thing is to move.
Sometimes it's to hold still and not run. Either way, the psalm says the strength is given: he shall strengthen thine heart.
Good courage, in this sense, isn't bravado. It's a first step taken by someone who believes they aren't taking it alone.

how: Christians turn to passages such as Joshua 1:9 and Psalm 27 before new beginnings and in hard seasons, and pray for strength to do what they fear.

games.q: you've been asked to give the toast at your brother's wedding, and your hands are already shaking. what did Joshua get that you could borrow?
o: an old promise, said again: you won't be alone.
a speech that made the fear disappear.
a good reason to hand the job to someone braver.
games.why: Joshua heard the promise Moses had already given him: “he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.” courage with company, fear and all.

practice: Name one brave thing within reach: a hard call, an apology, a no, asking for help. Then name the one thing most likely to stop you, and the very first step, nothing past it.
If you pray, you can borrow Joshua's words: be strong and of a good courage.
